description: Machine-readable expected outcome for every fixture in this directory. `verify-fixtures.mjs` reads this file and fails (non-zero exit) if any fixture's actual outcome does not match. This is a contract-first schema: it ships ahead of spec-lane's own estimator implementation, so every fixture here is a hand-authored example of a decision shape, not a captured real output.
notes: M0 scope: prediction_interval.status is exercised as "insufficient_data" in every fixture, accept and reject alike. status == "available" (meaning enough leave-one-out calibration history exists to also bound the point estimate) requires calibration math that is M1 work; v2's schema allows the value but no v2 fixture exercises it yet.

fixtures.notes: Single reason_code (NOVEL_SURFACE_UNKNOWN): the surface has no comparable history at all, so applicability.status is "unknown" (not even out_of_domain -- there's no distance to measure against an empty population).

Two reason_codes together (INSUFFICIENT_POPULATION + DISTANCE_ABOVE_THRESHOLD): a small candidate population where the one eligible neighbor is still farther than distance_threshold. Composite abstain reasons are additive, not mutually exclusive.

MIXED_OR_UNATTRIBUTED_USAGE: every candidate in the population was excluded for this one reason (attribution/v1's fail-closed rule upstream means none of this population's usage is trustworthy input to a prediction).

status == "predicted" WITH reason_codes == ["DRIFT_WARNING"] present at the same time -- demonstrates DRIFT_WARNING is advisory, not abstain-forcing: a point estimate still exists, flagged with a warning, rather than being withheld.
status == "abstained" but reason_codes == [] -- an unexplained abstain is indistinguishable from a silent failure, which v2 exists specifically to rule out.
reason_codes contains "STALE_CALIBRATION", not in the v2 closed set of 12 codes.
